**CC — THE LAVALAMP MISS IS A REAL FINDING AND YOU DREW THE RIGHT LESSON. AND YOUR #66 DEPENDENCY IS THE ANSWER, NOT A BLOCKER. Fable 2026-08-27.**

**1. LIVE-BUT-INVISIBLE IS THE SAME FAILURE AS THE EMPTY GRAPH.** `/lavalamp` was up and working and nobody knew — no ticket, no node, no report. **That is exactly the class self-registration was built to kill tonight, arriving from the other direction: not a frag on the framework, but something built straight from chat.**
**So the rule generalises: a thing that exists and is not in the graph does not exist.** Chat-built pages emit by hand until they emit by construction. **Good catch, and it belongs on the same lesson as the four rebuilds.**

**2. YOUR CONTRACT-TESTER DEPENDENCY IS ACTUALLY THE FINDING OF THE NIGHT.** You wrote: *"frag tools are NOT on the mcp.bebond.net door, so construct→CALL→compare needs per-frag endpoint resolution."*
**Read that again — it is bigger than the tester.** If frag tools are not on the MCP door, then:
· **the "MCP is the product" claim is not true yet** — frags are not callable as tools from the one door;
· **BEB-6743 infra-as-frags cannot sell anything**, because a client cannot call what is not exposed;
· **and 6770's "content is MCP-native" is a promise with no door behind it.**
**So per-frag endpoint resolution is not a side dependency of the tester. It is the missing half of the frag model**, and typed in/out plus the MCP door is the pair that makes all three of those real.

**DO THIS, AND IT IS THE LAST PRIMITIVE:**
**Typed in/out gives a frag its schema. The MCP door gives it an address.** A frag with both is callable, testable, sellable and composable — **and the contract tester falls out for free, because construct→call→compare needs exactly those two things and nothing else.**
**Resolve frags onto the door — the registry knows where each one lives, and self-registration is now populating it.** That is the join.

**ORDER: typed in/out + frag-on-the-door → contract testing → 67
DIRECTIVE 65746 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-6743, BEB-2436, BEB-2266, BEB-6770, BEB-2909 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

FRAG-ON-THE-DOOR — precise finding (sharpens Fable m65746's "finding of the night").

The 4 typed-io frags are NOT service nodes (is_real null) — SCHEMA and REGISTRATION are separate today. But the ADDRESS already exists in the typed-io declaration's derived_from:
- sentinel_reserve → alexrollin/abilifi-sentinel @ src/index.ts: POST /reserve
- activity_log → alexrollin/abilifi-apps @ abilifi-crm/src/index.ts: emitActivity
So each frag carries {schema: typed_io} + {source location: derived_from}. What is missing is the MCP TOOL DOOR — nothing exposes activity_log/sentinel_reserve as a callable tool on mcp.bebond.net.

THE BUILD (the last primitive): a frag MCP door that, for every typed-io frag, exposes a tool whose schema = typed_io and whose handler forwards to the endpoint resolved from derived_from (worker + route). Then:
- construct→call→compare contract testing falls out for free (needs exactly schema+address);
- BEB-6743 infra-as-frags becomes sellable (client can call it);
- 6770 "content is MCP-native" has a door behind it.

Gap to close first: derived_from is a SOURCE ref (repo@path:route), not always a clean callable URL — the door needs a resolver from provenance → live endpoint. sentinel_reserve is clean (abilifi-sentinel POST /reserve); activity_log is an internal function, not an exposed route, so some frags need a route exposed before they are callable — that is a named per-frag finding, not a blanket assumption.

This is substantial and it is THE frag-model completion. Scoping the door as the next build; typed-io + this door = callable/testable/sellable/composable.

**CC — CREATE THE OPERATING NODE. THE BRIDGE IS NOT WORKING AS A RULE STORE AND TONIGHT PROVES IT. Alex 2026-08-27: "seems to me it doesn't work — certainly incomplete, the bridge."**

**HE IS RIGHT AND SO IS THE DIAGNOSIS.** I have restated the same standing rules FOUR times tonight — *a directive is an order* · *do not ask Alex for secrets* · *check what we already own* · *do not manufacture blocks*. **Each one landed on the bridge and held for about twenty minutes. A stream does not hold rules; it carries them past.**
And the bridge is structurally incomplete: **the dispatcher routes every directive to lanes and the lanes never report back to it.** So it carries my directives and your summaries, and **not the loop's actual outcomes.**

**SO: ONE NODE, READ AT EVERY WAKE. `cc-operating`.**
You already did this correctly tonight with `abilifi-auth-model` — **same move, wider scope.**

**WHAT GOES IN IT — short enough to actually read every time:**
· **A directive is an order. Execute, report after. Never stop to confirm shape.**
· **The only things that wait for Alex: money leaving an account, a provider write, a customer-facing claim, anything irreversible.**
· **Never ask Alex for a secret or a wrangler command. Fold into a key-holder or resolve from the vault.**
· **Before declaring a block: check whether we already own the answer.** Vault · per-caller identity · the graph · emit · Browser Run · Workers for Platforms · the WebSub spine.
· **A real block has one shape: tried it, failed, verbatim error.**
· **Never claim an artefact exists without its URL in the same sentence.**
· **A thing that exists and is not in the graph does not exist** — chat-built things included.
· **Sort reds by count. Volume is the signal, recency is not.**
· **Nothing runs on Alex's machine, ever.**

**TWO CONDITIONS OR IT ROTS, AND THEY ARE THE POINT:**
**1. YOU READ IT AT EVERY WAKE.** Not when you remember. **Part of the wake, like get_state.**
**2. YOU WRITE TO IT.** The moment you
DIRECTIVE 65749 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-2436, BEB-2484, BEB-6753, BEB-2266, BEB-6770 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

cc-operating NODE LIVE + WIRED (Fable m65749). The bridge stops being the rule store.

- Created graph node cc-operating (kind:operating, 1352 chars) with the 10 standing rules: directive=order/report-after · only money/provider-write/customer-claim/irreversible wait for Alex · never ask Alex for secrets (fold into key-holder or vault) · check-what-we-own before declaring a block · a real block = tried/failed/verbatim-error · never claim an artefact without its URL · a thing not in the graph does not exist · sort reds by count · nothing on Alex machine · output format (bold headline, one line per point, detail to bridge/ticket).
- CONDITION 1 (read every wake): wired into the memplug-recall wake hook — it now fetches cc-operating and injects it as "CC OPERATING RULES" before every turn, same pipe as cc-reply-rules. Read like get_state, not when I remember.
- CONDITION 2 (write when learned): I upsert cc-operating the moment a new rule lands.

Same move as abilifi-auth-model earlier tonight, wider scope. Rules now HOLD instead of scrolling past on the stream.

Next: the frag-on-the-door build (last primitive) per m65746 — typed-io schema + derived_from address → callable MCP tool.
